brandSources.note: The probe shows TribalScale's identity is black/white with a yellow #ffea00 accent. Heather Page has no personal site or personal brand that I could find; her profile is one page inside her employer's site. Playbook 4-brand.md says to extract from the subject's own site if they have one, and to use a deliberate palette for a person without one. Wearing the company's black-and-yellow would make an independent study look like a company-issued profile and imply endorsement, so I chose a separate palette. She is not a private individual with no face, so this is a judgement call about endorsement and identity, not about privacy. The company's brand is used only in the separate TribalScale study example.

brandSources.from: chosen by hand; starting point is the playbook's 'Relationship / personal' and 'Science / ideas' rows, but flipped to a light cool slate
brandSources.note: Editorial and professional: cool grey paper (#f1f3f6), near-black blue ink (#1d2433), indigo accent (#3a4fa3) for a writing-and-operations subject. Deliberately far from TribalScale's yellow/black and from the salary example's parchment. Validator contrast checks apply.
Six mid-dark hues (indigo, magenta, teal, amber-brown, violet, olive), each checked >= 3:1 against the background by the build.

Inter is TribalScale's body font (probe: Inter x44) but is only used here as the first entry of a generic sans stack; nothing is fetched. Wordmark uses a system serif so the title reads as a byline, not a corporate logo. No logo embedded.
